focus: Angle 3: profiles, DSH_HOME and repo-local configuration
noveltyJustification: Five findings are new (project instruction chain, profile file list, no project config, patch overlay grammar, repo folder split); two extend known DSH_HOME and --patch facts.
answeredQuestions: What does the harness read from the working directory and `$DSH_HOME`, and what should a repo-local runtime folder contain?

label: The harness home resolves explicit config, then DSH_HOME, then ~/.dsh, treating a blank DSH_HOME as unset; the shared agents home resolves from DSH_AGENTS_HOME or ~/.agents and sits deliberately outside the harness home.

A profile is $DSH_HOME/profiles/<name> with cordis.yml, cordis.patch.yml, package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml plus shared profiles/node_modules; there is no project-level profile lookup, so a checkout cannot carry a profile.

Workspace instructions are the native project read: $DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md, then <agentsHome>/AGENTS.md, then every project candidate from the .git root to the cwd, with AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md base candidates and AGENTS.local.md/CLAUDE.local.md local overlays, deduplicated by content.

Each instruction chain gets its own maxBytes budget, 65,536 bytes in dsh-base, dropping broader files before truncating the most specific; loading refreshes on cwd change and first-party read/write/edit touches, never on shell navigation.

--patch <path> is the only repo-local configuration lever: a repeatable overlay applied after the profile layer with the same id/disabled/config row grammar, able to replace the default-model row, enable a route or disable a plugin per dispatch.

DSH_HOME can be relocated per lineage; pointing it at a lineage subdirectory produced a self-contained headless profile, session tree and storages with no dependency on ~/.dsh, which is the fan-out state-isolation mechanism and the reason the repo folder must not itself be DSH_HOME.

A .dsh/ repo folder has a smaller configuration surface than .pi/ or .hermes/: patches/ for overlays, SYNC.md, generated skills/agents/prompts trees, and a hand-authored plugins/ bridge, with no settings.json analogue because defaults are an agent-default-model row and settings persist into the active profile patch.

The Pi precedent splits generated from authored where the runtime forces it: agents and prompts generated, skills a whole-directory symlink, extensions hand-authored, settings/models/mcp hand-authored; Hermes generates markdown-only skill copies because its scanner quarantines symlinked trees.

reason: Profile lookup is DSH_HOME-only and a checked-in profile would need node_modules and a package install per checkout.
Settings persist through the active profile Cordis patch; defaults are an agent-default-model row.
